# Expected symbols from the zint test-suite (libzint, BSD-3-Clause, (c) Robin Stuart and contributors).
# Source: https://github.com/zint/zint, backend/tests/test_hanxin.c and test_2of5.c (function test_encode),
# master at f5fd98106d02644e742a7a794771b3e9f277dbca (2026-10-09). The `expected` module strings were copied
# unchanged; nothing was computed by BurnBurn. Cases are the ones with plain ASCII data, return code 0 and
# a symbol of at most 27 x 27 modules (Han Xin versions 1-3; larger versions are not implemented).
# hanxin case 1 is marked in zint as the ISO/IEC 20830 Figure 1 example ("Hanxin Code symbol", level 2).
# c25standard cases carry the zint remark that zint uses 4X start/end wide bars where BWIPP uses 3X.
# Extraction: a throw-away script (not kept) that tokenises the C initialisers; re-extract, do not edit by hand.
# Line format: <kind> <case number in zint> key=value... data=<hex of the input> bits=<modules, row-major, 1 = dark>
# ecc/ver/mask are zint's option_1/option_2/option_3 (-1 = automatic); `check=1` appends the mod-10 check digit.
hanxin 0 ecc=-1 ver=-1 mask=-1 mode=UNICODE_MODE width=23 data=31323334 
hanxin 1 ecc=2 ver=-1 mask=-1 mode=UNICODE_MODE width=25 data=48616e78696e20436f64652073796d626f6c 
hanxin 3 ecc=1 ver=1 mask=-1 mode=UNICODE_MODE width=23 data=31323334353637383930 
c25standard 0 check=-1 width=97 data=3837363534333231 bits=1111010101110100010101000111010001110101110111010101110111011100010101000101110111010111011110101
c25standard 1 check=1 width=107 data=3837363534333231 bits=11110101011101000101010001110100011101011101110101011101110111000101010001011101110101110100010111011110101
c25standard 2 check=-1 width=117 data=31323334353637383930 bits=111101010111010111010001011101110001010101110111011101110101000111010101000111011101000101000100010101110001011110101
